This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the William P. Hobby Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=khou

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official National Weather Service observations at Houston Intercontinental Airport recorded a daily maximum of 89°F on September 6, 2026, three degrees below the 1991–2020 normal and consistent with the presence of showers and thunderstorms that limited afternoon heating. This outcome produced the market’s near-certain 100% implied probability for the 88–89°F bin, as real-time surface data and model guidance converged on a suppressed high under increased cloud cover and moisture. Historical analogs for early September show that similar convective patterns frequently cap highs in the upper 80s rather than the low 90s typical of clear days. The result aligns with the skin-in-the-game consensus among traders monitoring National Weather Service reports, with only remote possibilities of revision arising from post-analysis quality control or station-specific discrepancies.

Official forecasts from the Korea Meteorological Administration and international models converge on a peak near 28–29°C (about 82–84°F) during afternoon hours, with minimal cloud cover and light winds limiting further warming or cooling. Recent observations show morning temperatures climbing steadily from the low 20s°C without significant model shifts or incoming fronts. eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models indicate a peak near 30°C on September 7 in Beijing, with rain arriving in the afternoon likely capping the high before it can climb much higher.** Multiple sources, including WeatherBug, Luft Time, and others, project highs of 29–31°C (84–85°F), consistent with the market’s leading outcomes at 29°C (26.5%), 30°C (36.0%), and 31°C (14.5%). 

This aligns with the approach of cooler air ahead of the White Dew solar term, which is bringing a small-to-moderate rain event starting midday or afternoon on the 7th. Precipitation and associated cloud cover are expected to limit solar heating and produce a noticeable drop to around 23°C on the 8th. 

The tight clustering of probabilities around 29–31°C reflects model agreement on modest daytime warming from current conditions (today’s high near 31°C) tempered by the timing of the rain, with limited upside beyond 32°C or downside below 28°C under the current setup. Updated model runs and official briefings from the Beijing Meteorological Bureau or China Meteorological Administration in the coming hours will provide the clearest resolution signals for traders.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Clear skies and light northeasterly winds shifting northerly are positioning Qingdao for a peak temperature near 28–29 °C on September 7, with model runs showing modest upside potential from strong September solar insolation and urban heat retention.** 

Low humidity (around 50–65 %) and minimal cloud cover limit evaporative cooling and allow surface heating to continue into early afternoon, while stable high pressure suppresses convective development that could cap the maximum. Small differences between 30 °C and 31 °C hinge on the precise timing of the wind shift and any late-day marine influence from the Yellow Sea, which official forecasts from sources such as the China Meteorological Administration and international models place in the upper 20s °C. Trader positioning reflects this narrow uncertainty band, with the market-implied odds capturing the limited but real chance of an extra degree or two under optimal clear-sky conditions before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from multiple models positions 32°C as the most probable high for Karachi on September 7, 2026, aligning with the market's leading 51.5% implied probability.** 

Current conditions feature high humidity (70-90%), moderate west-to-southwest winds, and partly cloudy skies typical of the post-monsoon transition, which moderate daytime heating along the Arabian Sea coast. Official and ensemble forecasts (including GFS-based outputs) consistently project afternoon maxima near 31-32°C (88°F), with limited model spread and no indications of stronger onshore flow or enhanced cloud cover that would suppress temperatures further. Historical September averages for Karachi hover around 31°C highs, providing a stable baseline. Traders appear to weigh these steady atmospheric conditions and the proximity to resolution against minor upside risks from clearer skies, supporting the tight clustering around 31-33°C outcomes. Updated model runs and local observations tomorrow morning will be key near-term catalysts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service and private model guidance points to a highest temperature in Miami on September 7 in the upper 80s to low 90s, driven by southerly flow under weak high pressure, high dew points near 78–80°F, and strong afternoon heating before scattered thunderstorms develop. This setup favors the market's leading 90–91°F bin by allowing peak readings before convective cooling sets in, consistent with late-summer climatology where Miami averages near 89–91°F. Elevated Gulf Stream sea-surface temperatures and moisture from nearby tropical systems like Hurricane Lana add humidity without introducing cooler air masses. Updated model runs and National Hurricane Center briefings through the evening of September 6 remain the key near-term catalysts that could shift implied probabilities if convection timing or steering changes.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Persistent warm air mass and clear to partly cloudy skies under light southerly flow are positioning the highest temperature in Austin on September 7 near the upper 90s.** Official National Weather Service guidance and multiple model runs forecast a daytime high of 96–99°F at Austin-Bergstrom and Camp Mabry, with afternoon peaks reaching 98–99°F under minimal cloud cover and dew points in the low 70s. This aligns with the market’s leading 98–99°F bucket at 47.5% implied probability and the secondary 96–97°F range. Recent Labor Day weekend readings in the mid-to-upper 90s, combined with only isolated shower chances below 10%, have reinforced trader confidence in above-average warmth relative to the 1991–2020 September 7 climatological high of 93°F. Light south winds of 3–6 mph and heat indices near 105°F further support limited mixing and strong daytime heating.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus around 13–14°C for São Paulo’s September 7 high reflects the arrival of a polar air mass that has sharply suppressed daytime temperatures across southeastern Brazil. Official forecasts from sources including Climatempo and numerical models show a cloudy, stable boundary layer with southeasterly flow limiting insolation and keeping maxima near 12–15°C, well below the month’s 23°C climatological average. Minor spread in the 13°C versus 14°C probabilities stems from small differences in cloud-cover timing and boundary-layer mixing within the latest model runs, with new observational data and updated guidance expected to refine the exact peak before resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 8 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Recent model consensus points to a peak temperature in Munich on September 8 driven by warm southwesterly flow, clear to partly cloudy skies, and strong daytime insolation under high pressure.** Multiple forecasts, including ICON, ECMWF guidance, and local outputs, indicate afternoon highs near 29–31°C (roughly 84–88°F), with hourly profiles showing peaks around 30–31°C under light winds and low humidity. This places the market-implied odds for 31°C (40.5%) and 32°C (36.5%) in close contention, reflecting small but meaningful differences in model timing of any residual cloud or exact boundary-layer mixing. Historical September averages hover near 21°C, so the current warm anomaly stems from a transient ridge rather than a prolonged heatwave. Traders are watching the next ECMWF and DWD runs for refinements, as even modest shifts in forecast maxima or dew points could tip probabilities between the two leading outcomes before resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Ben Gurion International Airport in degrees Celsius on 8 Sep '26.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecast guidance from models such as ECMWF and GFS, corroborated by Israeli Meteorological Service outlooks, points to a stable warm air mass with clear skies and light northwesterly winds supporting a daily maximum near 31–32°C in Tel Aviv on September 8. This aligns with late-summer climatology where highs average 29–31°C, though urban heat effects and afternoon insolation can push readings 1–2°C higher at official stations. Trader consensus favoring 33°C reflects expectations of modest model upward revisions or measurement variability, while lower probabilities for 34°C or above account for the low likelihood of significant warm advection or reduced cloud cover before resolution. Updated model runs and IMS observations over the next 48 hours will refine these implied odds.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Vnukovo International Airport in degrees Celsius on 8 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=UUWW

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from Russian meteorological services and international models indicate a cool air mass over Moscow for September 8, with daytime highs most likely between 13–18 °C amid variable cloud cover and light northwest winds. This positioning reflects a transient dip following warmer late-summer conditions, consistent with climatological September averages near 18 °C but tempered by current steering patterns and limited diurnal heating. Model consensus clusters around 14–15 °C maxima, though slight differences in cloud timing or boundary-layer mixing could shift the peak by 1–2 °C. Updated runs from Hydromet and global ensembles expected in the next 24–48 hours will refine resolution criteria for the daily high. Trader-implied odds near 14–15 °C align with this narrow forecast range and inherent short-term uncertainty.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble and deterministic model runs from sources like ECMWF and GFS show Istanbul reaching a daytime maximum of 24–25°C on September 8 under mostly clear skies and persistent northeasterly flow of 15–25 km/h. This pattern, typical for early September, limits strong surface heating while suppressing cloud cover and precipitation, keeping the thermal profile close to climatological norms of 23–26°C. Trader positioning at 61% implied probability for 24°C reflects the tight clustering of these forecasts, with only modest upside risk from any late warming in the boundary layer. Updated high-resolution guidance issued in the next 24–48 hours will be the key catalyst for any shift in odds.

Updated NHC and local radar data tomorrow morning will refine resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecast guidance for Panama City, Panama, points to peak temperatures near 33–34 °C on September 8, with model consensus tempered by widespread diurnal convection and elevated humidity during the Central American rainy season. Abundant low-level moisture from the Pacific and Caribbean, combined with light steering winds, favors scattered showers and cloud build-up by midday that reduces surface insolation and caps afternoon maxima. Historical September climatology shows typical highs of 30–32 °C, but recent days with slightly clearer skies have allowed brief spikes toward 33 °C, supporting the near-even market split between the two leading outcomes. Any reduction in convective coverage or stronger subsidence could push readings to 35 °C or higher, while heavier or earlier rain would favor 32 °C or below. Official station data and updated model runs tomorrow morning will resolve the final maximum.
